# Paths and Project Roots {#chp:paths}

Paths are a quiet source of bugs. Extensions come in odd shapes, `~` expands
differently across systems, and a document in a subfolder sees the world from
a different working directory than a script at the top. The recipes here make
paths predictable.

## Take apart and rebuild extensions {#sec:file-ext}

`file_ext()`, `sans_ext()`, and `with_ext()` get, drop, and swap the extension
of a path. They understand double extensions such as `.tar.gz` and `.nb.html`,
which `tools::file_ext()` splits differently:

```{r}
p = c("report.Rmd", "archive.tar.gz", "notes.nb.html", "script.R")
file_ext(p)
sans_ext(p)
with_ext(p, ".html")
with_ext(p, c(".pdf", ".zip", ".html", ".txt"))
```

The last call shows that `with_ext()` is vectorized over the new extension too.

## Normalize and compare paths {#sec:normalize}

`normalize_path()` wraps `normalizePath()`, always uses `/`, and does not fail
on paths that do not exist. `same_path()` compares two paths after
normalizing both, so you do not need to care how each was written:

```{r}
normalize_path("~")
same_path("~/foo", file.path(Sys.getenv("HOME"), "foo"))
```

## Find files relative to the project root {#sec:from-root}

Inside a document in `docs/`, the data folder is one level up. Counting `../`
by hand breaks as soon as the document moves. `from_root()` returns a path
relative to the project root, which `proj_root()` detects for you:

```r
# in docs/report.Rmd, this returns ../data/cars.csv
from_root("data", "cars.csv")
```

## Find a file by name, wherever it lives {#sec:magic-path}

If you only remember the name of a file, `magic_path()` finds it anywhere under
the project. You can then move files around without breaking references:

```r
# finds data/raw/survey.csv wherever it lives
magic_path("survey.csv")
```

## Work in another directory for a moment {#sec:in-dir}

`in_dir()` switches the working directory, evaluates an expression, and then
goes back, even if the expression fails:

```{r}
in_dir(tempdir(), {
  writeLines("hello", "tmp.txt")
  file.exists("tmp.txt")
})
file.exists(file.path(tempdir(), "tmp.txt"))
```

## Create a directory only if needed {#sec:dir-create}

`dir_create()` returns `TRUE` when the directory exists or has just been
created, and it creates parent directories by default. No more warnings from
`dir.create()` about existing folders:

```{r}
d = file.path(tempdir(), 'a', 'b', 'c')
dir_create(d)
dir_create(d)  # already there, still TRUE
```

## Check if a directory exists {#sec:dir-exists}

`dir_exists()` is a vectorized test for directories:

```{r}
dir_exists(c(tempdir(), file.path(tempdir(), 'nope')))
```

## Check if a file exists, but not a directory {#sec:file-exists}

Base `file.exists()` says `TRUE` for directories too. `file_exists()` only
accepts real files:

```{r}
f = tempfile()
write_utf8('x', f)
x = c(tempdir(), f)
file.exists(x)
file_exists(x)
```

## Keep only the files that exist {#sec:existing-files}

`existing_files()` is `x[file.exists(x)]`. With `first = TRUE` it returns the
first hit, handy for a list of candidate config locations. It errors if none
exist, unless `error = FALSE`:

```{r}
f = tempfile()
write_utf8('x', f)
x = c('no-such-file.txt', f)
existing_files(x)
existing_files(x, first = TRUE)
existing_files('no-such-file.txt', first = TRUE, error = FALSE)
```

## Remove a directory only if it is empty {#sec:del-empty-dir}

`del_empty_dir()` checks for files and subdirectories first and deletes the
directory only when nothing is inside. It silently does nothing for `NULL` or a
missing directory:

```{r}
d1 = tempfile(); d2 = tempfile()
dir_create(d1); dir_create(d2)
write_utf8('x', file.path(d2, 'keep.txt'))
del_empty_dir(d1)
del_empty_dir(d2)
dir_exists(c(d1, d2))
```

## Tell absolute paths from relative ones {#sec:abs-rel-path}

`is_abs_path()` treats a leading `/` or `~` as absolute (and drive letters and
UNC prefixes on Windows). `is_rel_path()` is its negation:

```{r}
x = c('/usr/bin', '~/notes', 'data/a.csv', '../up.txt')
is_abs_path(x)
is_rel_path(x)
```

## Check if a path is inside a directory {#sec:is-sub-path}

`is_sub_path()` tests whether each path starts with the directory path. It is a
plain string comparison, so normalize both sides with `normalize_path()` first
if they may be written differently:

```{r}
is_sub_path('a/b/c.txt', 'a/b')
is_sub_path('a/b/c.txt', 'd/b')
```

## Spot URLs among paths {#sec:is-web-path}

`is_web_path()` flags paths starting with `http://`, `https://`, `ftp://` or
`ftps://`, so you can treat local files and remote resources differently:

```{r}
is_web_path(c('https://www.r-project.org', 'www.r-project.org', 'img/a.png'))
```

## Tell files from directories in messages {#sec:mark-dirs}

`mark_dirs()` appends a slash to directories, which makes listings easier to
read. Relative paths are tested against the working directory, so use full
paths or `in_dir()`:

```{r}
d = tempfile()
dir_create(file.path(d, 'sub'))
write_utf8('x', file.path(d, 'a.txt'))
mark_dirs(list.files(d, full.names = TRUE))
```

## Guess the MIME type of a file {#sec:mime-type}

`mime_type()` uses the **mime** package when installed, else the system `file`
command. Either way you get a type like `text/html` for each path. Results from
the command are cached, because running it is slow:

```r
mime_type(c('index.html', 'logo.png', 'script.R', 'data.csv'))
# "text/html" "image/png" "text/plain" "text/csv"
```

Files without an extension (such as `Makefile`) get `empty`, which defaults to
`text/plain`. Set `empty = NA` (with `use_mime = FALSE`) to ask the system
command instead.

## Express a path relative to a directory {#sec:relative-path}

`relative_path()` works out how to get from a directory to a file, using `..`
when needed:

```{r}
relative_path('foo/bar.txt', 'foo/')
relative_path('/a/b/c.txt', '/d/e/')
relative_path('/a/b/c.txt', '/d/e/', use.. = FALSE, error = FALSE)
```

With `use.. = FALSE`, a path outside `dir` cannot be made relative; `error =
FALSE` returns it unchanged instead of failing.

## Teach `proj_root()` about your own project type {#sec:root-rules}

`proj_root()` walks up from a path until a rule matches. `root_rules` is the
default rule matrix: column one is a regex for file names, column two a regex
for the file content (empty matches anything). By default it recognizes R
packages (`DESCRIPTION` with `Package:`) and RStudio projects (`.Rproj`). Add a
row to support another marker, here a `project.toml` file:

```r
root_rules
#>      file            pattern
#> [1,] "^DESCRIPTION$" "^Package: "
#> [2,] ".+[.]Rproj$"   "^Version: "

rules = rbind(root_rules, c('^project[.]toml$', ''))
proj_root('~/work/myproj/src/deep', rules)  # ~/work/myproj
```

`proj_root()` returns `NULL` if no ancestor matches. Note the file regex is
matched with `list.files()`, which skips hidden files such as `.git`.
